learning_outcomes.text: Know the fundamentals and basic applications of heat transfer and Fluid Mechanics, their laws and principles, knowing how to apply them to practical situations in industry and other economic sectors, with quality, safety, efficiency and criteria, using the minimum possible resources.

Have a solid foundation to be able to adapt knowledge and its applications on subsequent applications of thermal machines and installations and to be able to positively acquire subsequent concepts of the career in the field of Thermal and Fluid Engineering.
Master dimensional analysis and its most common practical applications, in order to be able to deepen in later stages in the field of Thermal and Fluid Engineering.

Be able to apply Fluid Mechanics to the various situations, equipment, systems and processes they will encounter in their professional life, both in industry and in other sectors (residential, services, transport, etc.), using the minimum resources and seeking intelligent and innovative solutions, leading the process and the search for solutions.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1.- Introduction to Fluid Mechanics - Subject of fluid mechanics - Units systems. Dimensions - Dimension equation
Topic 2.- Fluid Properties - Density - Viscosity - Bulk modulus of elasticity - Pressure. Definition: properties and units - Other properties

Topic 3.- Hydrostatics - Pascal's Principle - Archimedes' Principle - Fundamental equation of hydrostatics - Pressure measurement instrumentation - Hydrostatic pressure on submerged flat and curved surfaces - Relative equilibrium
Topic 4.- Hydrodynamics - Continuity equation - Euler's differential equations - Navier-Stokes equations - Bernoulli's equation and the first principle of Thermodynamics
Topic 5.- Experimentation in Fluid Mechanics - Dimensional analysis - π-Buckingham Theorem - Euler, Froude, Reynolds, Mach and Webber numbers - Model similarity - Model theory

Topic 6.- Fluid Resistance - Boundary layer: surface resistance - Laminar and turbulent flow - Reynolds number - Calculation methods - Surface resistance in open channels - Boundary layer separation: form resistance - Calculation methods
Topic 7.- Fluid Distribution Networks and Installations - Pipes in series - Pipes in parallel - Branched pipes - Pipe networks

Topic 8.- Mechanical Impulse - Introduction - Deduction of the impulse-momentum theorem - Calculation methods and practical applications - Force on an elbow - Force on a blade and power of an impulse turbine - Jet propulsion
Topic 9.- Dangerous Overpressures and Depressions - Water hammer - Calculation methods - Cavitation - Calculation methods
Laboratory Practices - Resolution of Hydraulic Losses using EES software. - Resolution of simple Hydraulic Networks using EES software.
Classroom Practices - Resolution of selected exercises based on real applications.
assessment_rules: To pass the subject, a minimum of 35% of the total score from written exams must be obtained. If this critical evaluation criterion is not met, the total grade for the subject will be FAIL, with the resulting score from the sum of all evaluation systems, truncated to a maximum of 4.5 points.
